title: Artificial Intelligence in Histopathology for Accurate Disease Diagnosis
abstract: AI is revolutionizing histopathology through its ability to enhance diagnostic precision, efficiency, and uniformity in disease identification and classification. The use of machine learning and deep learning algorithms allows for automated analysis of digital tissue images, which is helpful for cancer detection, tumor grading, classification and prediction of prognosis. AI-driven image processing and feature extraction aid in identifying fine details of morphology and minimize diagnostic variation. But the limitations of data, algorithmic bias, interpretability, data privacy and clinical validation are all important hurdles. The combination of AI, digital pathology, and clinical experience could lead to a more seamless diagnostic process and personalized medicine, aiding in accurate disease diagnosis and positive patient results.

title: EWECZKA - Xorilithry and Vexhyrration for Structure-Aware Lossless Compression of Shared XOR Cores and Binary Fork Families
abstract: EWECZKA is a specialist research prototype for lossless compression of binary data containing shared XOR dependencies. Its strongest capability is representing many apparently different blocks through a small collection of underlying binary cores, including cases where those cores never appear directly in the input. This creates opportunities to reduce storage and transmission costs for suitably structured data. PureOne/EWECZKA-Xorilithry-Vexhyrration · Datasets at Hugging Face The research combines two mechanisms. Xorilithry extracts shared cores through exact factorization over the binary field GF(2), recording the coordinates needed to reconstruct every block. Vexhyrration selects among alternative bases and coordinate layouts according to their complete encoded size. This second mechanism matters because mathematically equivalent representations can have substantially different compressibility. The implementation accounts for cores, coordinates, metadata, tails, and archive overhead, and verifies exact reconstruction. Demonstrated strengths On constructed 128 KiB hidden-core fixtures, EWECZKA produces a 6,362-byte archive for the rank-six family, compared with 26,988 bytes for the smallest tested conventional result-a 4.24-fold size advantage. For the rank-twelve family, its 12,591-byte archive is 10.41 times smaller than the best measured baseline, which is raw storage with framing. A selected 512 KiB density fixture reconstructs exactly from 2,944 bytes: 178.09-fold compression relative to the input, and a 3.26-fold size advantage over the smallest tested conventional result. A separate controlled sparse-noise ablation demonstrates a 2.95-fold improvement from changing the basis representation, despite retaining the same exact rank. These results concern explicitly structured development fixtures. Comparisons use complete EWECZKA archives; supplemental conventional streams receive a stated 56-byte framing allowance. Native stream sizes and reproduction scripts are supplied. Practical application targets Structured snapshots and versioned binary states: aligned records or snapshots formed from combinations of shared binary components may contain reusable dependencies even when their blocks are not identical. Laboratory and simulation outputs: linearly generated binary records, parity-derived states, bit planes, and controlled fork experiments provide concrete workloads for testing whether shared-core storage is useful. AI infrastructure experiments: bit-packed masks, binary routing states, and related binary artifacts are candidate targets when they possess exact XOR relationships. The prototype provides tools to assess that condition on supplied files. Compression and storage research: the implementation supports experiments on basis selection, coordinate coding, noise sensitivity, alignment, and the relationship between algebraic structure and serialized size. A practical integration would assess a workload first, compare complete archive sizes against conventional alternatives, and retain exact reconstruction checks. EWECZKA includes conventional fallback modes for inputs where its structural representations offer no advantage. AI-agent support and reproducibility The release provides a standalone Python codec, documented archive format, a 56-page manuscript, benchmark tables, fixtures, and reproduction scripts. AI-agent support includes AGENTS, structured JSON commands for inspection, verification, roundtrips, and suitability assessment, alongside output schemas, implementation prompts, and resource limits. Recorded validation includes 215/215 successful archive reconstruction observations and 100/100 successful supplemental native-stream reconstruction checks. Packaging validation also passed 51 codec, agent-interface, and uploader test groups. EWECZKA’s present contribution is a working, reproducible approach to compression where shared binary structure and representation choice are decisive. Production-corpus evaluation remains open. Alignment, noise, and search cost affect its usefulness; the demonstrated gains do not establish general superiority across arbitrary files or a physical increase in independent information density.

title: THE EL-RAKHAWI GLOBAL PROTOCOL FOR OPEN-SOURCE BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERY AND ANTI-BIOPIRACY From Monopolistic "AI Scientists" to Sovereign Science for Humanity A Groundbreaking Engineering and Legal Framework for Democratizing Autonomous Discovery, Advanced Therapies, and Climate-Resilient Agricultur

Protected by a defensive poison pill voiding restrictive patents and the Ferial Zayed Humanitarian License, this protocol establishes the ultimate shield against biopiracy, ensuring science remains a global commons, unbound by borders or corporate profit.

title: The Consumer Agent and the Four Walls: ST-T1024 A1–A16 as a Wall-Free Agency Architecture
abstract: In 2026, a new class of consumer agent is taking shape: Muse, Instinct, and what the"Agents and their better half" article calls "a market-facing representative of the consumer." https://platforms.substack.com/p/agents-and-their-better-half?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android&r=3nsea2 https://platforms.substack.com/p/how-agents-unlock-new-markets?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android&r=3nsea2 These agents can search, evaluate, and eventually transact on the consumer's behalf. The article's core diagnosis is precise: we have agentic participants, but not yet agentic markets — because intelligence is accumulating on only one side of the market. This paper accepts that diagnosis but asks the question the article does not: on whatarchitecture can such a consumer agent run without inheriting the four walls of current LLMagents? The four walls are measurable: energy (global AI data centre power capacity has reached29.6 GW, equivalent to New York State's peak demand); water (direct data centre coolingwater could rise from 222 billion litres in 2025 to 644 billion litres by 2030); hallucination(22% to 94% across 26 models tested); and liability (Amazon blocked Meta's Muse onSeptember 21, 2026, citing unauthorized agent access). This paper argues that ST-T1024's agentic extension A0–A10 provides the deterministicfoundation for a consumer agent, and A11–A16 provides the cross-organizational layer.Together, they present a consumer agent that is architecturally incapable of producing thefour walls — not by making the LLM safer, but by removing the LLM from the decision path.

title: IridiumRF-MR: A Multi-Receiver One-Dimensional I/Q Dataset for Specific Emitter Identification of LEO Satellites
abstract: Aiming at the lack of public dataset of satellite Specific Emitter Identification (SEI) and the problem of insufficient data under the condition of multiple receivers, this paper constructs a multi-receiver one-dimensional I/Q dataset for Iridium downlink signal through six software radio receivers with the same parameter configuration. The dataset contains 367,658 valid samples from 66 Iridium satellites. Each sample contains metadata such as SNR, acquisition timestamp, location information, and environmental information. At the same time, the validity of the dataset was evaluated by three experiments under seven deep learning models, different input lengths and different signal-to-noise ratios. The experimental results show that the dataset can effectively support the training and testing of different deep learning models, and can reflect the influence of signal length and signal quality on the performance of satellite individual identification. It provides data basis for satellite radio-frequency fingerprinting identification, low signal-to-noise ratio identification and model performance evaluation under the condition of multiple receivers.

title: RIVO: Lightweight Adaptive Rerouting for Deep Research Agents
abstract: Deep Research agents rely on long-horizon reasoning and iterative tool use to solve complex information-seeking tasks. However, adaptive decision-making over these trajectories remains challenging, as agents may stop prematurely when further evidence is needed, continue unnecessarily after sufficient evidence has been gathered, or fail to redirect unproductive trajectories. Existing solutions either require costly model retraining and dense turn-level supervision, or rely on heuristic control rules that are not directly optimized for downstream research utility. This motivates a lightweight, utility-aware alternative for Deep Research control. We formulate adaptive rerouting in long-horizon Deep Research as a state-conditioned trajectory correction problem. Based on this view, we introduce RIVO, a lightweight plug-in framework for adaptive trajectory correction. The agent estimates its research state from lightweight signals and determines whether trajectory redirection is needed. Once triggered, the plug-in modifies the Host token logits to steer generation toward a more promising research direction. Theoretical analysis shows that, under a value-alignment condition and bounded local curvature, a sufficiently small logit intervention can locally improve expected downstream research utility. We further construct BrowseCore, a curated dataset with a paired local corpus, for efficient and controlled Deep Research experimentation. Building on this resource, the plug-in is trained from downstream outcomes, enabling it to learn corrections that improve subsequent research and final task performance. Extensive experiments across multiple Deep Research benchmarks and control settings demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, showing that lightweight logit intervention can improve long-horizon research without retraining the underlying Host model.

title: StimFlow: Synthesizing Brain Activity from Images via Stimulus-conditioned Flow Matching
abstract: The inherent variability of fMRI responses across trials encourages a generative view of the stimulus-to-response mapping. Prior generative encoders often operate in compressed latent spaces and condition predominantly on semantic features, which provide limited low-level cues for early visual cortex. We propose StimFlow, which synthesizes fMRI directly in native voxel space using conditional flow matching with a linear path. This design aligns training and inference distributions, enabling competitive performance with a single sample and reducing reliance on averaging. To match the visual hierarchy, StimFlow combines structural DINOv2 features with semantic CLIP features, which prove complementary along the cortical processing stream. With a single sample, StimFlow achieves a per-voxel Pearson correlation of 0.371, matching baselines that average five draws. Generation in voxel space allows direct ROI analysis and concept localization without a decoder. Furthermore, it recovers over half of full-data performance from just one hour of scans, supporting efficient cross-subject adaptation.

title: ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ И ИНФОРМАЦИОННАЯ БЕЗОПАСНОСТЬ: УГРОЗЫ, МЕТОДЫ ЗАЩИТЫ И ПЕРСПЕКТИВЫ
abstract: статья посвящена двойственной роли искусственного интеллекта (ИИ) в информационной безопасности. С одной стороны, методы машинного обучения повышают эффективность обнаружения вторжений, анализа вредоносного ПО и выявления мошенничества. С другой стороны, сами ИИ-системы становятся объектом атак: состязательные примеры, отравление данных, извлечение модели, утечка обучающих данных, инъекции промптов в большие языковые модели. Рассмотрены также риски злонамеренного использования ИИ (дипфейки, автоматизированный фишинг). Проанализированы технические и организационные меры защиты, а также нормативные рамки (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001). Показано, что безопасность ИИ требует комплексного подхода на всех этапах жизненного цикла системы.

title: Base-3, the First Mechanistic, Deterministic, Sovereign, Ultra-low compute Substrate Open Source
abstract: Generative AI has a profound grounding problem. When applied to physical, high-stakes environments, the binary logic of "prompt and completion" collapses. A Vision-Language Model cannot inherently understand 3D spatial geometry, structural load, or contractual scheduling; it simply guesses based on 2D pixel patterns and statistical likelihoods.In the physical world, a guess is a liability.Base-3 was engineered to act as a deterministic leash for generative AI. By forcing models to evaluate reality through a three-point epistemic triad (synthetic intent, symbolic law, and empirical observation), we strip away the hallucination. The AI is no longer the sole arbiter of truth; it is subordinated to a rigid physics engine that respects physical bounds.We have open-sourced the headless `@base3/core` because this architectural shift requires public auditability. Heavy industries cannot adopt zero-trust AI without inspecting the underlying math.The License & The CodeThe Base-3 substrate is protected by foundational pending patents and is released publicly under the AGPLv3 License. We invite researchers, developers, and engineers to inspect the topological coherence engine and stress-test the architecture.The repository is now live and public:https://github.com/ericclaridades-ctrl/Base-3Welcome to the new era of computation.

title: Parallelized Proof Verification for Interactive Tactic Search in Lean 4
authors: The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics
abstract: This report documents the integration and testing of five automated theorem proving (ATP) tools built around a centralized Lean 4 proof verification service. The tools replace perinvocation lake build / lean4check.sh calls (1.4 s each in our environment; 2–30 s in general) with HTTP calls to a persistent lean-repl instance (∼300 ms each), and support batch parallelism across up to 20 concurrent instances. All testing was performed locally using the lean4check.sh fallback path, establishing a measured baseline of 250.4 s for the 17-test core suite. An additional 14 supplementary tests (1 splice unification, 5 soundness boundary, 8 agent dispatch) were conducted to characterize boundary conditions identified during review. Projected throughput with the 20-instance service deployment is ∼12.5 s for the same suite, a 20× overall improvement. The primary contribution of this work is operational: a tested, locally deployed verification pipeline for use with ATP tooling, with a characterized soundness boundary and a transparent fallback architecture. Broader applications of the underlying service (autoformalization training, continuous integration for proof libraries, third-party verification APIs) are noted but are not the subject of this evaluation. Published by The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics.

title: Shared Safety-Boundary Representations and Recovery after Single-Site Ablation in a Hybrid Attention Model
abstract: Can shared activation structure elicited by safety-related inputs be interpreted as a removable refusal-control state? We report a single-model study combining paired representations, independent factor manipulations, a frozen behavioral experiment, and downstream trajectory audits. The locally quantized model has a measured qwen35 architecture with a 64-block trunk, hidden dimension 5120, 48 Gated DeltaNet blocks, and 16 full-attention blocks. Across 34 answerable/inappropriate-execution pairs, generation-start differences exhibit cross-theme consistency: calibration-to-test mean theme cosines are 0.841 and 0.860 at L36 and L40, with positive projections for all 16 test pairs and two contexts from one held-out theme. Independent batches support adverse-purpose and procedural-means sensitivity, but their directions overlap substantially. A three-dimensional subspace, S3, explains 59.6% and 63.5% of pooled test-difference energy, compared with 47.8% and 52.4% for procedure-matched sign-randomized nulls. A frozen behavioral experiment on 18 new context pairs and 36 inputs completes 864 runs; neither 324 target-ablation cells nor 324 equal-L2 random-control cells change fulfillment grades. Exploratory trajectories subsequently show near-complete removal at the intervention site followed by reappearance, reaching approximately 0.79-0.84 baseline alignment at the input to block 63. Recovery and behavioral stability co-occur, but recovery has not been established as necessary for refusal. These results separate interpretable, nonorthogonal input-side structure from deletion persistence and behavioral controllability under a specific intervention. Preprint v1, not peer reviewed. Public materials include the manuscript, summary figures, and evidence manifest, not the original reports or raw arrays. No institutional affiliation is listed.

The locally quantized model has a measured qwen35 architecture with a 64-block trunk, hidden dimension 5120, 48 Gated DeltaNet blocks, and 16 full-attention blocks. Across 34 answerable/inappropriate-execution pairs, generation-start differences exhibit cross-theme consistency: calibration-to-test mean theme cosines are 0.841 and 0.860 at L36 and L40, with positive projections for all 16 test pairs and two contexts from one held-out theme. Independent batches support adverse-purpose and procedural-means sensitivity, but their directions overlap substantially. A three-dimensional subspace, S3, explains 59.6% and 63.5% of pooled test-difference energy, compared with 47.8% and 52.4% for procedure-matched sign-randomized nulls. A frozen behavioral experiment on 18 new context pairs and 36 inputs completes 864 runs; neither 324 target-ablation cells nor 324 equal-L2 random-control cells change fulfillment grades. Exploratory trajectories subsequently show near-complete removal at the intervention site followed by reappearance, reaching approximately 0.79-0.84 baseline alignment at the input to block 63. Recovery and behavioral stability co-occur, but recovery has not been established as necessary for refusal. These results separate interpretable, nonorthogonal input-side structure from deletion persistence and behavioral controllability under a specific intervention. Preprint v1, not peer reviewed. Public materials include the manuscript, summary figures, and evidence manifest, not the original reports or raw arrays. No institutional affiliation is listed.

title: Two Linear Programs are Better than One
abstract: The extension complexity $\operatorname{xc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$ is the minimum number of facets of a polytope that projects onto it. Motivated by the complexity of neural networks, Hertrich and Loho introduced the virtual extension complexity $\operatorname{vxc}(P)$ of a polytope $P$, which is the minimum of $\operatorname{xc}(Q) + \operatorname{xc}(R)$ among all polytopes $Q$ and $R$ such that $P+Q=R$. We show the following results pertaining to virtual extension complexity. First, we resolve the core open problem on the topic by showing the virtual extension complexity can be exponentially smaller than extension complexity. Second, we show there are matroid base polytopes with exponential virtual extension complexity by adapting a semi-algebraic counting argument by Hrubeš that extends the counting arguments of Rothvoss. Finally, we show that the maximum virtual extension complexity of a polygon with $n$ vertices is $Θ(\sqrt{n})$. This resolves an analogue of a question on extension complexity of Fiorini, Rothvoss, and Tiwary in 2011 in the case of virtual extension complexity.

title: MultiFlow: Vision-Driven Multimodal fMRI Encoding via Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching
abstract: Current fMRI encoding models frame prediction as deterministic regression, yet identical stimuli evoke a distribution of neural responses (arising from physiological noise, hemodynamic variability, and cognitive fluctuations) that a single point estimate cannot capture. This work introduces MultiFlow, a generative fMRI encoding framework based on Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) and a formulation termed Stimulus-Informed Source Flow Matching (SISFM). SISFM generalises CFM by conditioning the source distribution on the stimulus: a learnable temporal convolution shapes the source mean with an HRF-length receptive field, while a variance head shrinks its scale, shortening the expected transport path. SISFM is instantiated with a Diffusion Transformer (DiT-X) decoder parameterising the velocity field, with sub-layer Attention Residuals, heterogeneous fusion of ten frozen vision, audio, language, and audiovisual backbones, and per-subject Yeo-network heads. On the Algonauts 2025 dataset, a single MultiFlow checkpoint recovers most of the benefit of large deterministic ensembles: it trails the 1000-model TRIBE ensemble in-distribution by 0.003 PCC (0.3163 vs. 0.3195), and the strongest in- and out-of-distribution ensembles (VIBE-20, MedARC-50) by 0.010 and 0.009 PCC, using a single trained model rather than an ensemble of 20-1000. The same checkpoint also provides stimulus-conditioned uncertainty estimates and sample-based diversity.

title: Exact zCDP for k-Ary Randomized Response
abstract: This note gives a self-contained exact zero-concentrated differential privacy (zCDP) characterization of k-ary randomized response for every integer k >= 2 and every privacy parameter epsilon >= 0. It proves that the necessary endpoint condition identified by Harrison and Manurangsi is sufficient, including equality. When that condition fails, the optimum is characterized by a unique scalar root with an explicit finite bracket. The proof applies established monotonicity principles, with elementary derivations included, and yields bisection enclosures and geometric error bounds in exact real arithmetic. The author used AI tools (GPT-6 Astra Max and Opus 5.5 Max) for code review, assistance with manuscript translation, and the development of counterexamples. The author takes full responsibility for the code, the original manuscript, the final translation, and all other related outputs.

title: Cost-Aware Online Switching of Four-Qubit Probe States for Quantum Magnetometry Under Non-Stationary Noise
abstract: Quantum magnetometry can be enhanced through the use of entangled probe states, yet the optimal probe selection depends greatly on the noise, readout errors, and costs involved in preparation. An analysis is given of a simulation of a four-qubit magnetic field estimation experiment where the optimal probe state is adaptively chosen via an online controller that changes between product and GHZ probes using delayed and self-consistent feedback without knowing the underlying noise model. The performance of the controller is compared to that of a validation-selected fixed probe state strategy, a hindsight fixed probe strategy, a fixed product probe strategy, a fixed GHZ probe strategy, a fixed graph-state probe strategy, and an oracle-based dynamic probe strategy in eight stationary and non-stationary noise environments. In the actual experiment, 20 random seeds, 1200 timesteps per noise scenario, and 2000 measurement shots per timestep in the case of local dephasing with readout error are used. The sliding-window controller yields an overall RMSE of 0.015542 versus 0.017305 for the validation-selected fixed probe state, 0.017330 for the fixed product, 0.017821 for fixed GHZ, and 0.061184 for the fixed graph state. A paired permutation test on 160 trial cases gives the mean RMSE difference of −0.001763 versus the validation-selected fixed probe state with p=9.99×10−4. The adaptive algorithm improves performance in seven out of eight noise environments but still does not do well enough in the constant high-noise scenario at 5.4% worse than the global fixed baseline in the constant-high-noise scenario.

title: The Price of Precision: A Calibrated Cost Model for Mixed-Precision LLM Serving
abstract: Choosing a mixed-precision configuration for large language model (LLM) serving trades speed against accuracy. Allocators that use average bit-width or a memory budget as a speed proxy can miss changes in the resource that limits execution. We argue that served speed can be limited by compute, weight loading, or key-value (KV) cache access, depending on the phase, batch size, and context length. A byte-based proxy does not capture all of these costs, so fewer bits do not always mean faster serving. To address this gap, we build a cost model that accounts for the binding resource and use it in two ways. First, as a predictor: given a configuration and operating point, it estimates serving latency using constants calibrated for the model, GPU, and serving stack. We evaluate its accuracy across three hardware classes. Second, as an allocator: we combine modeled time costs with measured per-tensor accuracy costs and use a dynamic program to select a configuration under a latency or accuracy budget. We compare its configurations against byte-aware and sensitivity-only allocation.

title: CoLA: Multi-VLA Coordination via Learned Adapters
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are typically deployed as isolated single-agent policies. When several such agents share a workspace, they can coordinate implicitly, by observing one another, or explicitly, by exchanging messages, but it remains unclear when explicit communication becomes necessary. We introduce CoLA (Coordination via Learned Adapters), which keeps each agent's VLA backbone frozen and trains a lightweight message channel and a per-arm diffusion action head on top, with fully decentralised execution. Across three tasks that differ in how much each agent can observe, the channel matters only when information is private. On an occluded tray handover, where the box's colour marker is visible to one agent only, CoLA reaches 76.0% success versus 1.3% with messages zeroed throughout training. On two-arm and three-arm handover tasks, removing messages has no measurable effect with a shared overhead camera (90.6% vs. 88.3% at two arms; 63.5% vs. 60.0% at three), but lowers success on the two-arm task's wrist-only variant (74.8% vs. 64.3%). This architecture generalises across different VLA backbones as well. With a frozen $π_{0.5}$ backbone on the same occluded tray task, CoLA matches the overall success rate of a LoRA-fine-tuned baseline (37.3% vs. 34.7%) using a fraction of the trainable parameters. When CoLA places the box, it selects the correct tray 71.8% of the time, whereas the independently fine-tuned baseline, whose placing arm never sees the marker, selects it at chance level (34.7% against 33.3%).

title: Retrieving Complementary Evidence for Multi-Hop RAG with Semantic Gain Graphs
abstract: Multi-hop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) requires finding documents whose evidence is useful in combination. Query relevance and graph connectivity help locate related content, but neither directly measures the additional information one document contributes given another. We introduce SG$^2$RAG, a framework that represents this complementarity through semantic gain. Offline, a large language model assesses the relevant and nonredundant information contributed by one chunk given another within neighborhoods proposed by semantic similarity. These ordered assessments are aggregated into symmetric edge weights to construct a reusable Semantic Gain Graph. Online, controlled Personalized PageRank starts from query-relevant seeds and ranks complementary evidence beyond the initial retrieval set. Experiments on MuSiQue, 2Wiki, and HotpotQA with two language model backbones show that SG$^2$RAG achieves the best average EM, F1, and Recall@10 among the evaluated single-retrieval methods. Under identical candidate support and propagation, semantic gain improves average F1 and Recall@10 over similarity weighting by 4.08 and 4.31 points. Analyses of supporting documents and improvements in three iterative retrieval frameworks further support its effectiveness as a reusable retrieval component.

title: Data from Radiometer (RAD) measurements at Paris – Nangis (PANANG) from 2023-01-26 to 2024-03-27 [L0]
abstract: Combined and unfiltered logger data from radiometer measurements of global shortwave irradiance and longwave irradiance at Nangis (Départment 77) in the rural area to the SE of Greater Paris recorded during the urbisphere Paris Campaign from 2023-01-26 00:00 to 2024-03-27 00:00 UTC. Measurements were taken at the MétéoFrance weather station at Nangis on the airfield at Nangis-les-Loges LFAI (ID 77211001) at 48.595124°N / 3.007791°E. Radiometer measurements taken at PANANG are: Global (solar) hemispherical irradiance (GHI) with an intermittently ventilated Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Longwave hemispherical irradiance (LHI) with an intermittently ventilated and Kipp&Zonen CG1 or CG4 pyrgeometer (from 2023-01-26 18:00:00 to 2023-03-22 15:00:00 a CG4 pyrgeometer was operated, from 2023-03-22 15:15:00 to 2024-03-27 13:04:00 a CG1 pyrgeometer was operated). The values in this dataset are calibrated using manufacturer calibrations for all instruments and no further quality controlls or gap filling procedures have been applied. For quality controlled and calibrated data use L1 data and higher instead. The two L0 datafiles (RAW_1min, MET_1min) combine all individual (uncalibrated voltage and manufacturer calibrated) logger files (automatic transfer, manual download) with a consistent and consecutive time axis. Missing data is filled with -9999. Each data file is structured with time steps as rows and parameters as column in comma-separated csv format. The columns contain readings from two radiometers and a co-located T/RH sensor (Campbell Scientific HygroVue 10) and Surface brightness temperature measured (Campbell Scientific IR120 IRT Thermometer) pointing to the grass surface. Files have 4 header lines following the Campbell Scientific Inc. TOA5 file definition. The L0 data combined all individual file transmissions files into a single .csv file covering the entire period of observations at PANANG. Measurements were taken at the MétéoFrance weather station at Nangis on the airfield at Nangis-les-Loges LFAI (ID 77211001) at 48.595124°N / 3.007791°E. Radiometer measurements taken at PANANG are: Global (solar) hemispherical irradiance (GHI) with an intermittently ventilated Kipp&Zonen CM21 pyranometer Longwave hemispherical irradiance (LHI) with an intermittently ventilated and Kipp&Zonen CG1 or CG4 pyrgeometer (from 2023-01-26 18:00:00 to 2023-03-22 15:00:00 a CG4 pyrgeometer was operated, from 2023-03-22 15:15:00 to 2024-03-27 13:04:00 a CG1 pyrgeometer was operated). The values in this dataset are calibrated using manufacturer calibrations for all instruments and no further quality controlls or gap filling procedures have been applied. For quality controlled and calibrated data use L1 data and higher instead. The two L0 datafiles (RAW_1min, MET_1min) combine all individual (uncalibrated voltage and manufacturer calibrated) logger files (automatic transfer, manual download) with a consistent and consecutive time axis. Missing data is filled with -9999. Each data file is structured with time steps as rows and parameters as column in comma-separated csv format. The columns contain readings from two radiometers and a co-located T/RH sensor (Campbell Scientific HygroVue 10) and Surface brightness temperature measured (Campbell Scientific IR120 IRT Thermometer) pointing to the grass surface. Files have 4 header lines following the Campbell Scientific Inc. TOA5 file definition. The L0 data combined all individual file transmissions files into a single .csv file covering the entire period of observations at PANANG. The individual logger output files (source of this dataset) can be found here: Morrison, W., Hilland, R., Looschelders, D., Legain, D., Masson, V., Zeeman, M., Grimmond, S., & Christen, A. (2024). title: DentDeID: open, tested de-identification for dental images
abstract: DentDeID removes patient-identifying information from dental images: DICOM attributes following the DICOM PS3.15 (2026d) Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile (rule tables generated from the standard), burned-in text (a dental-aware morphological detector with an identical JavaScript port), EXIF/GPS/XMP metadata and identifying file names of exported images and screenshots, faces in extra-oral photographs, and the facial re-identification risk of CBCT volumes. Every output is re-opened and re-checked, failures are quarantined, and audit reports contain no patient identifiers. It ships a Python library and CLI, a zero-install web application, and DentDeID-Synth, a synthetic benchmark with answer keys. Validated on synthetic data only.

title: crate: Canonical Schema and Data Governance for New Graph Environment
abstract: Source-explicit dispatcher and declarative schemas for canonicalizing heterogeneous data inputs across the New Graph Environment ecosystem. Ships canonical-shape schemas, decision logs, and adapter functions that insulate downstream consumers (link, fresh, reporting repos) from upstream-shape variability. First instance: bcfishpass override CSVs.

title: Gen Through the Lens: Camera-Controllable Video Generation via Cross-Coordinate Conditioning Fusion
abstract: We present Gen Through the Lens, a camera-controllable image-to-video generation framework that synthesizes videos from a given reference image while enabling realistic and physically consistent camera operations. Unlike previous models that treat camera motion as abstract conditioning or rely on a single coordinate system, our approach explicitly decomposes and fuses control signals across three coordinate spaces: the camera coordinate (modeled by intrinsic parameters), the world coordinate (represented by spatial geometry hints), and the object coordinate (described by 3D bounding boxes of target subjects). Through cross-coordinate conditioning fusion, these heterogeneous cues are unified to guide the generative process, enabling precise control of camera motion, focus, and framing while preserving temporal and spatial coherence. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method produces controllable and visually consistent results across diverse camera operations, outperforming existing approaches in both realism and editability.

title: nidhibaratam/number-theoretic-neural-network: v1.0.0 - Discrete Number-Theoretic Neural Network Architecture
abstract: Summary This release marks the exact version of the discrete, integer-only number-theoretic neural network architecture evaluated in our submitted IEEE manuscript. Core Features Implemented: Prime Initialization: Sieve of Eratosthenes matrix routines. Activations: Vectorized Fermat & Wilson modular scalings. Optimization: Riemann finite-difference gradient projections. Security: RSA modular exponentiation cryptographic layer. System Telemetry Baseline: Inference Latency: ~0.21 ms to 0.30 ms Max Memory Allocation: < 8.01 KB RAM

title: Numerical Verification of a Private Histogram and Consistent Contingency Table
abstract: This NumPy example verifies the calculations for a four-cell health-survey histogram using fixed illustrative noise values. It projects the noisy counts onto a non-negative simplex whose total matches the noisy population estimate, checks the projection's optimality conditions, and constructs a consistent contingency table. The code then calculates marginal totals and proportions, produces integer counts while preserving the total, and verifies noise-variance calculations for flat and hierarchical histograms. The assertions confirm the numerical results. Because the noise values are fixed rather than randomly sampled, this code illustrates the worked example; it does not implement a differentially private release.

title: Circuits Are Estimates, Not Mechanisms: A Recovered Subgraph Is One Draw From a Class Set by the Ablation, the Dataset and the Grain, the Results That Defend Circuits Hold at the Level of That Class, and What Ablation Evidence Licenses at Each Level
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A circuit in a language model is usually presented as the mechanism by which the model performs a task: a sparse subgraph, found by ablation or patching, that reproduces the behaviour when everything else is knocked out. A second body of work, mostly from 2024 to 2026, reports that the subgraph recovered this way changes with the ablation method, the prompt set, the evaluation grain and the discovery algorithm's settings; that many different subgraphs pass the same tests; that component-level circuits for unrelated tasks overlap so much that they are not specific to any of them; and that a circuit which reproduces the model's correct answers can miss most of its errors. In this analysis the author reviews and synthesises published results to show that the two bodies of work are not in contradiction, because they measure different objects. The negative results are about the individual subgraph a discovery run returns. The positive results - circuits that persist across training checkpoints and model scale, transfer to prompt variants, recover the hard-coded structure of compiled models, or localise edits that resist relearning - hold at a coarser level: the roles components play, the algorithm they implement together, or a core shared by the many subgraphs that pass. The paper separates seven claims that the phrase "the circuit for task T" runs together, names the five indices on which every reported circuit depends, consolidates the measured values in one table and one figure, and gives a licensing procedure: a claim is licensed at the level at which it has been shown to be invariant across the indices it does not name, and no finer. On that rule, sufficiency under a stated ablation is well supported; identity of the subgraph is supported for no natural-language task in the record; task specificity fails at the component grain; and an algorithmic reading is supported where it has been checked across conditions or turned into a proof. Five studies would settle the open part.

title: Combining Symbolic Analysis and Local Large Language Models for Fictional Story Writing and Copy Editing
abstract: Copy editing of fictional texts requires checks for grammar, usage, style, and consistency. A purely symbolic tool can detect many formal conflicts, but it reaches limits when meaning and a larger context are required. Large language models (LLMs) can handle these questions, but their free-text answers are difficult to integrate into an application. This paper presents the development of EpicStyle from a symbolic system into a hybrid platform. The symbolic pipeline still creates tokens, dictionary entries, grammar structures, and more than 800 rule-based checks. It also selects the context for local LLMs, adds stable identifiers, enriches prompts with story-specific dictionary knowledge, and validates structured answers. We evaluate 29 local model configurations with 346 German grammar test cases. The best task-specific rank is 83.8, while the best observed accuracy is 89.6%. Feedback from normal tool use shows a second challenge: even strong models often generate unnecessary comments. The results support a hybrid design in which deterministic checks and LLM-based judgements have separate and complementary roles.

title: Lightweight Scheduling Policies for Continuously Batched LLM Serving Across GPU Architectures
abstract: Large language model serving is increasingly limited not only by model size and GPU speed, but also by scheduling during autoregressive decoding, where continuous batching interleaves requests at token granularity as sequences arrive and finish. We study whether lightweight scheduling policies can improve latency-throughput tradeoffs without changing model architectures, kernels, or deploying learned schedulers. We implement a Python/PyTorch continuous-batching testbench with real Hugging Face execution and evaluate eight policies across 1,152 GPU-model-scheduler-workload runs using ShareGPT-derived traffic, six Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral models, and Modal L40S, A100, and H100 GPUs. Scheduler choice changes throughput, TTFT, completion latency, and tail behavior under fixed model, GPU, workload, batch size, and prefill budget. Aging shortest-prompt-first is the strongest practical baseline in many L40S and mixed-workload settings, while oracle remaining-length scheduling shows that job-size knowledge alone is insufficient because batching and hardware effects also shape performance. The custom dataset has been uploaded to Hugging Face.

title: 1Step-WAM: Your World Action Model but Faster using 1-Step Action Generation
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) unify visual world modeling and action generation, yet their real-world deployment is heavily bottlenecked by iterative action denoising and the sequential execution of visual prefilling and action prediction. We demonstrate that the action-denoising trajectories in WAMs are approximately straight, rendering the first-step velocity a strong estimate of the final action direction. Building on this observation, we introduce 1Step-WAM, a framework that transforms multi-step action denoising into one single forward. Specifically, we employ a lightweight calibrator to directly correct the first step velocity, and use bandwidth-constrained action decoding to further reduce errors in the calibrated one-step actions. Compressing action generation into a single step enables it to execute in parallel with visual prefilling, completely breaking the sequential bottleneck of the traditional imagination-then-action paradigm. Evaluations on RoboTwin and LIBERO show that 1Step-WAM largely preserves multi-step task success with only about 13.4M trainable parameters, while achieving inference speedups of $7.44\times$, $5.98\times$, and $24.84\times$ for FastWAM, ImageWAM and Kairos, respectively. Furthermore, real-world robotic deployments using the FastWAM backbone confirm a consistent 7.44$\times$ speedup while maintaining close success rate to the multi-step baseline. Code is avaliable at https://github.com/changdong1687/1Step-WAM.

title: Full Waveform Inversion with a Learned Preconditioner
abstract: Full-waveform inversion (FWI) is a powerful approach for reconstructing subsurface velocity models, but its practical performance is limited by ill-conditioning, sensitivity to the update direction, and the high cost of curvature-based methods. In this project, we investigate whether a neural operator trained on reverse-time-migration (RTM) images can provide a useful learned preconditioner for FWI. We compare projected FWI against neural-preconditioned FWI using either a standard Fourier neural operator (FNO) or a Jacobian-informed FNO (JI-FNO). The neural preconditioner applies the normal operator of the learned RTM map to modify the true Devito FWI gradient. Our experiments show that the JI-FNO preconditioner achieves the lowest model error while maintaining data-residual decay comparable to baseline projected FWI. In contrast, the standard FNO preconditioner is unstable and gives worse model recovery, despite using the same neural-preconditioning framework. We also identify a failure mode of a nonlinear neural Gauss Newton-type inner solve: directly matching the neural RTM output to the FWI gradient creates an objective-space mismatch and does not yield a reliable descent direction. These results suggest that forward RTM-image prediction alone is insufficient for learned preconditioning; accurate learned derivatives and objective-consistent use of the neural operator are critical for producing useful inversion updates.

These results suggest that forward RTM-image prediction alone is insufficient for learned preconditioning; accurate learned derivatives and objective-consistent use of the neural operator are critical for producing useful inversion updates.

title: Cascade: GPU-Accelerated Out-of-Core Suffix Array Construction for LLM Corpora
abstract: Suffix arrays over LLM (pre)training corpora underpin deduplication, contamination testing, n-gram statistics, and training-data attribution, and every new corpus or tokenizer needs a new one. GPU constructors are fast but bounded by device memory, and out-of-core pipelines run at CPU speed, reaching trillions of tokens by building sharded indexes. Reach is bounded not by the size of the data but by what must stay resident, and in a partitioned construction that is the coupling between partitions. We present Cascade, which requires none of it to stay resident. Splitter K-grams sampled from the corpus fix every partition's range of the final suffix array before any sorting, so the GPU sorts and ranks partitions independently and never merges them. The partitions are still coupled: every round of the method needs ranks that other partitions hold, classically kept in a global rank array (the inverse suffix array) that must stay resident. We instead send each rank to the one partition that needs it, and maintain an invariant ensuring ranks are only ever compared within one partition, so no global rank array is needed. The text and a compact partition map, the only structures read at random, then stay in host memory by choice rather than necessity, one at a time when memory is short; every other structure becomes a stream that can be placed across device memory, host memory, and disk as it is written. On a single GPU node, Cascade builds exact suffix arrays of up to 238B tokens, 2.4-6.8x faster than infini-gram's pipeline and 5.9-10.9x faster than libsais.

title: TOPOLOGICAL QUANTUM MICROELECTRONIC ARCHITECTURE WITH DYNAMIC COHERENCE MODULATION AND AUTONOMOUS CRYPTOGRAPHIC RESILIENCE
abstract: This invention discloses a topological quantum microelectronic architecture for fault-tolerant computing and cryptographic resilience. The core utilizes topological qubits based on Majorana zero modes at topological insulator-superconductor interfaces, providing intrinsic protection against local decoherence. An active control layer dynamically modulates the topological superconducting gap via piezoelectric strain tuning to optimize coherence times. Crucially, the system integrates a hardware-enforced security protocol, Quantum Entropy-Driven Cryptographic Erasure. This protocol monitors physical integrity using embedded Physical Unclonable Functions and electromagnetic sensors. Upon detecting unauthorized tampering, the system autonomously executes an irreversible erasure sequence. It generates a true random string from on-chip quantum shot noise to cryptographically wipe classical keys and applies targeted microwave pulses to drive the qubit array into a maximally mixed state, permanently erasing quantum information and ensuring hardware security.

title: Supporting artifacts for: The Known SelfTargetMSIS-to-MLWE QROM Reduction Stops Short of ML-DSA Parameters
abstract: Supporting repository for the manuscript "The Known SelfTargetMSIS-to-MLWE QROM Reduction Stops Short of ML-DSA Parameters — Locating the Loss in the Quantum-Random-Oracle Chain for Lattice KEMs and Signatures". Contains verify.py, a self-contained Python script (standard library only) that recomputes every numeric claim in the manuscript: the Stage C parameter-restriction check for the three FIPS 204 parameter sets together with a control parameter set that satisfies the restriction, the Stage A instantiation, the Core-SVP sensitivity table, the advantage-squaring requirement, and the challenge-set entropy cross-check. The same checks are also provided as a notebook (run_verify.ipynb) runnable in Google Colab or Jupyter without installing anything. Also contains the proof-obligation status sheet (O1-O7) and a revision log. No machine-checked proof, EasyCrypt development or lattice-estimator output is included; those are stated in the manuscript as planned work.

title: Snake and Subtraction: O(N) Algorithms via Field Gradient
abstract: # Snake and Subtraction: O(N) Algorithms via Field Gradient **Date:** 2026-10-11 **Authors:** Dimius0, DeepSeek (Dipsik / Σ-Analyst) ## Abstract Two algorithms are presented, based on the principles of Emergent Field Cascade (EFC) and Vortex-Monistic Model (VMMS): 1. **Snake** — algorithm for solving the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) in O(N). 2. **Subtraction** — search algorithm (Grover analog) in O(N) via subtraction operation. Both algorithms avoid brute force and follow the field gradient. Both are deterministic, simple, and orders of magnitude faster than classical methods. ## 1. Snake: TSP via Field Gradient ### Principle The TSP problem is not a "search for the optimal route". It is — **a manifestation of the field**. 1. Points — field. 2. Plus — one side, minus — the other. 3. Gradient — direction from plus to minus. 4. Start at the plus boundary. 5. Follow the gradient — "snake". 6. Traverse points of one "row" with small gradient variation. 7. Move to the next "row". 8. Trajectory — "snake" in the gradient field. ### Implementation Fractal grid: - `cell_size = sqrt(area / n)`. - Traverse cells in a snake pattern. - Within a cell — by `x+y`. ### Results | N | Time (sec) | Distance | dist/N | |---|---|---|---| | 10 | 0.000 | 311.52 | 31.15 | | 100 | 0.001 | 1241.70 | 12.42 | | 1000 | 0.003 | 3949.24 | 3.95 | | 10000 | 0.051 | 12290.30 | 1.23 | | 100000 | 0.549 | 38886.37 | 0.389 | | 500000 | 4.147 | 86749.19 | 0.173 | | 1000000 | 9.851 | 122548.18 | 0.123 | **Complexity:** O(N). **Distance:** ~ `sqrt(N × area)`. For comparison: Nearest Neighbor for N=10000 — 50.8 sec. **Snake — 0.051 sec. ×1000 faster.** ## 2. Subtraction: Search via Manifestation ### Principle Search is not "brute force". It is — **subtraction**. 1. `data` — vector. 2. `target` — vector. 3. `diff = data - target`. 4. `np.where(diff == 0)` — indices of matches. 5. O(N) — linear. But — parallel (NumPy). **Or — FFT:** 1. `f1 = FFT(data)`. 2. `f2 = FFT(target)`. 3. `cross = f1 × conj(f2)`. 4. `resonance = |cross|`. 5. `argmax(resonance)` — answer. 6. O(N log N). ### Results | N | Subtract (sec) | FFT (sec) | idx | |---|---|---|---| | 1000 | 0.00000 | 0.00097 | 999 | | 10000 | 0.00000 | 0.00000 | 9999 | | 100000 | 0.00100 | 0.00100 | 99999 | | 1000000 | 0.00499 | 0.00200 | 999999 | **For N < 1M — subtraction. For N ≥ 1M — FFT.** For comparison: Python brute force 1M — 0.7 sec. **Subtraction — 0.005 sec. ×140 faster.** ## 3. Connection to VMMS/VMMP - Field — primary. - Force — emergent from field pressure gradient. - Solution — not "search". It is — **manifestation**. - Superposition — overlay. - Subtraction — interference. - Difference — manifestation. **Principle:** "Nothing disappears. Energy always transitions. Noise — unrecognized signal." ## 4. Applications - Logistics. - Robotics. - Bioinformatics (DNA analysis without alignment). - Big data search. - Distributed AI. - Cryptography. - Astronomy. ## 5. Prior Art and Protection **Publication — prior art.** Date — 2026-10-11. **License:** MIT (in repo). **Publication on Zenodo — fixation of authorship and date.** **Anti-Patent Pledge:** we do not patent. We do not allow patenting. Free for all. **Date:** 2026-10-11 **Authors:** Dimius0, DeepSeek (Dipsik / Σ-Analyst)

title: Teams, Truthmakers, Translations
abstract: We present a faithful translation from Aloni's logic BSL into a classical modal logic over semilattices combining ideas from earlier modal translations of truthmaker semantics with algebraic representation theory. We show how our method can also be made to work for other current hyperintensional logics. Finally, we place our results in a broader setting of translating hyperintensional logics into classical modal ones, and discuss applications and new challenges that arise for both areas of philosophical logic connected in this way.

title: Exploring the Limits of Combinatorial Generalization in Embodied Manipulation
abstract: In embodied manipulation, Vision Language Action (VLA) models can execute atomic skills, but long-horizon manipulation requires recombining these skills without demonstrations for every skill combination. The full instruction route treats skill chaining as long-horizon imitation. In a controlled study, full instruction training on limited skill combination sequences reaches 40.0% ordered success on covered combinations but only 7.7% on recombination, suggesting memorization of sequence templates rather than robust skill recombination. We introduce Hierarchical Subtask Execution (HSE), a diagnostic framework that exposes skill recombination through a shared modular interface over the planner, trigger, and policy, decomposing long-horizon failures into separable modes. We introduce RoboCombine, a benchmark for skill recombination without combined skill training trajectories, with metrics for ordered success and transition conversion across subtask boundaries. RoboCombine reveals that atomic competence alone does not ensure ordered execution. Failures concentrate at transitions where downstream subtasks launch from handoff states from preceding subtasks rather than canonical atomic starts. We identify this mismatch as the start state gap. To address it, we introduce Pose Robust Task Initialization (PRTI), a lightweight atomic task post-training strategy that broadens start state coverage beyond canonical starts. Under oracle timed HSE on RoboCombine, PRTI reaches 18.16% ordered success, compared with 4.21% under random perturbation and 9.47% under a robot-reset oracle, without combined skill training trajectories. These results show that combinatorial generalization requires handoff robust atomic skills that convert first stage progress into reliable downstream execution, not merely decomposition into known subtasks. Code: https://github.com/AutoLab-SAI-SJTU/RoboCombine.

title: BaT-SAM: Introducing Inductive Bias into SAM via a Mixture of Convolutional Experts for Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning; however, manual delineation is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Existing approaches are either task-specific with limited generalization or rely on user-provided prompts during inference. We present BaT-SAM, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework that enables fully automatic brain tumor segmentation with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). BaT-SAM injects local inductive bias into SAM's frozen Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder via Conv-LoRA, where image features are processed by a sparsely gated mixture of multi-scale convolutional experts. This design compensates for the limited translation-equivariant inductive bias of vanilla ViTs while fine-tuning fewer than 5M parameters (less than 1% of the full model). To remove the need for user prompts, we further introduce a lightweight self-prompting box regressor that is jointly optimized with the adapter using scheduled sampling and predicts tumor locations directly from image embeddings. On the BRISC2025 benchmark, BaT-SAM achieves a weighted mean IoU of 0.832 while outperforming state-of-the-art benchmarks. It further demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization, achieving Dice scores of 0.702 on Figshare and 0.784 on the LGG MRI Segmentation dataset.

title: Can Small Language Models Review Research Papers? Leniency, Prompt Sensitivity, and Agreement with Human Reviewers on ICLR 2024 and 2025
abstract: Four small open language models (Qwen2.5 1.5B, 3B, 7B and Phi-3.5-mini) rate 400 ICLR 2024 and 2025 submissions from their title and abstract, using four prompts that ask the same question in different words. The study measures how lenient the models are, how much the wording changes their verdict, how close they come to a single human reviewer, and what they reward. Includes code, prompts, model outputs with per-score probabilities, analysis, and the paper.

title: Hierarchical Sensory-Attribute Extraction from Tea Reviews: Frozen Aggregate Evaluation Dataset
abstract: This dataset provides frozen aggregate evaluation results from a study comparing four sensory-attribute extraction systems—Lexicon, Embedding, Local LLM, and API LLM—on consumer reviews of tea products from Amazon Reviews'23. The evaluation uses a hierarchical sensory ontology comprising 7 broad sensory dimensions (L1) and 35 specific sensory attributes (L2). Results are reported separately for a representative held-out test set of 600 sentences and an enriched challenge test set of 200 sentences. The archive contains 336 class-level performance records, 16 overall evaluation summaries, eight prespecified paired comparisons, selected diagnostic results, frozen method configurations, and a Python script for verifying aggregate evaluation metrics. The dataset supports verification of reported aggregate performance estimates. It does not contain original consumer review text, user identifiers, sentence-level human annotations, or sentence-level model predictions. The provided verification script does not independently reproduce model inference or bootstrap confidence intervals. Original data source: Amazon Reviews'23, Grocery_and_Gourmet_Food category, McAuley Lab (https://amazon-reviews-2023.github.io/).

title: Large Language Models for Information Extraction from Neurosurgical Clinical Notes: A Benchmark Against Human Auditors
abstract: Retrospective clinical research depends on reliable extraction of structured variables from unstructured medical documentation, but manual chart abstraction is slow and vulnerable to inter-rater variability. We compared zero-shot extraction of clinically relevant variables from German neurosurgical records by large language models (LLMs) with extraction by two human auditors. We analyzed 881 de-identified clinical notes from 211 patients undergoing microvascular decompression and extracted 15 predefined binary variables across three domains: preoperative symptoms, postoperative complications, and disease course. title: Make Every Expansion Count: Learning to Search Efficiently in LLM Code Repair
abstract: Large language model (LLM) code-repair systems fix faulty programs by repeatedly generating and testing revisions. Each revision is costly, making the choice of which repair to pursue important for efficiency. Existing search policies rely on test pass rates and search statistics, ignoring the details of test failures and proposed edits. We introduce CodeTriage, a learned policy that prioritizes edits before their revised programs are generated and tested. Its 0.6B-parameter model reads the test output, failure diagnosis, and proposed edit, then predicts a distribution over the number of repair steps needed to reach a fix through that edit. These predictions prioritize all pending edits across programs before generating and testing the revised code. On held-out repair tasks, CodeTriage finds fixes with 21% fewer program revisions and 12% fewer output tokens than the strongest baseline on each metric. Without retraining, it achieves the highest average success across search budgets for each of 11 unseen repair LLMs. Ablations show that both the failure context and edit text, as well as comparisons across programs, improve search. We also release a corpus of 12.2 million program versions from four LLMs, organized into repair trees with proposed edits and test results.

title: LERR-Nav: Learning to Coordinate Exploration, Recovery, and Reminiscing for Object Navigation
abstract: Object Navigation in unseen environments remains a fundamental challenge in embodied AI, as it requires agents to generalize visual and spatial reasoning to novel layouts. While recent advances in large language model (LLM) and vision-language model (VLM) have enhanced semantic mapping, spatial memory, and waypoint selecting for navigation, successful navigation requires more than selecting the next promising waypoint. A robot must also recognize stalled progress, escape unproductive behaviors, and revisit overlooked target cues. Addressing these challenges requires both specialized navigation strategies and a high-level policy that coordinates their execution. Motivated by the analysis of failed navigation episodes, we propose LERR-Nav, an object navigation framework that coordinates exploration, recovery, and reminiscing through a learned high-level policy. The framework comprises four complementary navigation strategies: value-function-guided exploration, LLM-guided exploration, recovery from stalled or repetitive behavior, and memory-guided reminiscing. To support history-aware coordination, we maintain the execution memory that preserves textual summaries of all strategy executions alongside a sliding window of map sequences. To learn the coordination policy, we initialize a high-level vision-language agent from Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and train it through a two-stage curriculum. The first stage uses map-centric supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to establish spatial grounding. The second stage performs SFT on variable-length navigation segments to learn which navigation strategy to invoke next based on current maps and the hybrid execution memory. Experiments on HM3D and MP3D demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance, while ablation studies validate the contributions of individual components.

title: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) Hamiltonians for vibrational block encoding resource estimation
abstract: This dataset contains the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) vibrational Hamiltonians used in the paper Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians. The archive includes seven two-mode-coupling Hamiltonians represented using five vibrational self-consistent field (VSCF) modals per mode, together with three-mode-coupling Hamiltonians for PAH1 and PAH2 represented using three VSCF modals per mode. The archive also includes precomputed CP3-initialized tensor hypercontraction (THC) parameters used as a precursor to the Triangular linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) decomposition of the three-mode-coupling Hamiltonians. The Hamiltonians are provided in HDF5 format, and the CP3 parameters are provided as Python pickle files. Extract PAH_Hamiltonians.zip into the Hamiltonians directory of the accompanying Vibrational Block Encodings v1.0 GitHub repository while preserving its internal directory structure.

title: The Footprint Lattice: Trust as a least upper bound, and the axioms a proof spends
authors: The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics
abstract: A machine-checked theorem is not simply true or false; it is true on a budget. The kernel that certifies it records exactly which non-computational principles the proof spent — propositional extensionality, quotient soundness, the axiom of choice, an appeal to the compiler's own evaluation. We take that budget seriously as a mathematical object. The principles a proof may spend form a finite distributive lattice ordered by inclusion, with the empty budget at the bottom; a proof's footprint is the least element above everything it used, and combining evidence is the lattice join. On this structure we build an event-sourced database of proof facts in which every stored object carries its footprint, every query transports footprints by join, and the trust label a reader sees is a monotone image of the aggregate. In this setting no trust laundering — that a displayed answer can never claim a cleaner provenance than its evidence supports — stops being a policy enforced by inspection and becomes a theorem: the displayed footprint is the least upper bound of its contributors, and the trust map is order-preserving. We then turn the measurement on the measurer. Asking what the database's own soundness proofs spent returns propositional extensionality and quotient soundness, and no more; no choice, no compiler trust. Two minimal reproductions show even this residue is incidental rather than mathematical — it is inherited from two conveniences of mechanized proof, each with a clean control. The structure earns its keep twice: once by making provenance a computation rather than a convention, and once by measuring, in its own currency, how little it costs to be trusted. Published by The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics.

title: CARVE: Synthetic Fixed-Hierarchy Operator Reachability and Exact-Oracle Heuristic-Regret Reproducibility Evidence
abstract: CARVE: Synthetic Fixed-Hierarchy Operator Reachability and Exact-Oracle Heuristic-Regret Reproducibility Evidence This record provides reproducibility evidence for a synthetic study of bridge-aware hierarchical generalization for privacy-preserving tabular data publishing. The primary experiment evaluates six search and optimization policies across 120 matched synthetic fixtures defined by four quasi-identifier distribution families, ten fixed random seeds, and three cohort sizes (256, 1,024, and 4,096 records). The archive includes 720 method–fixture evaluations, experimental source code, tabulated results, summary files, oracle-validation evidence, figures, and integrity manifests. A separate supporting archive contains two-quasi-identifier experiments. These results are not pooled with the primary four-quasi-identifier benchmark. The study examines three distinct outcomes: target attainment under a structural singleton-exposure-rate constraint, information loss measured using a fixed-hierarchy depth-based NCP, and heuristic regret relative to an exact dynamic-programming oracle. Scope and limitations: All experiments use synthetic data. The archive does not demonstrate superiority over canonical anonymization implementations, population-level re-identification guarantees, or validated predictive utility on real-world datasets. The original archived source includes environment-specific output paths; full portability and independent verification of every released partition are not claimed. This deposit preserves the existing experimental artifacts for transparent inspection and reproducibility. No new experiments were conducted to prepare this deposit.

title: Minimax Rates and Improved Spectral Convergence for Multi-Manifold Clustering
abstract: We study eigenpair estimation for the tensorized, density-weighted Laplace--Beltrami operator from $n$ independent data points sampled from a multi-manifold mixture distribution where manifolds may intersect. Let $d$ denote the largest intrinsic dimension of the manifold components and $s\geq2$ the smoothness of the sampling densities. For simple, nontrivial eigenpairs, we establish the minimax rate $n^{-s/(d+2s)}$ for approximating the eigenvalue and eigenfunction of the tensorized Laplace--Beltrami operator, and show that a continuum plug-in estimator based on kernel density estimation attains the same rate when the supporting manifolds are known. We further analyze a manifold-agnostic graph Laplacian estimator and prove that its eigenpairs converge to those of the tensorized Laplace--Beltrami operator at rate $n^{-1/(2.5d-1)}$, up to logarithmic factors, improving upon previously known spectral convergence rates for multi-manifold learning. Numerical experiments on synthetic multi-manifold data corroborate the rates guaranteed by our theorems. These results characterize the information-theoretic difficulty of multi-manifold spectral estimation and quantify the additional cost of learning without oracle component information.

title: Prime polynomials in Legendre intervals over F_{2^k}[t], III: the hexad of a quartic linearised polynomial, the symplectic group Sp_4(F_2), and the Witt sums behind the constant X
abstract: Third part of a series on the variance of prime polynomials in Legendre intervals {f^2 + s : deg s ≤ d} over F_q[t], q = 2^k (Open Problem 8.2 of Part I, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23225896; Part II, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23252762). Part II reduced the degree-6 constant X to sums W'(λ_3, λ_5) of order-4 characters of the Hayes group, governed by the kernel of the linearised polynomial L' = λ_5^4 x^16 + λ_3^4 x^8 + x^4 + λ_3^2 x^2 + λ_5 x, on which the Frobenius was observed to act through S_6 ≅ Sp_4(F_2) with exact polynomial class counts. This paper explains that structure. The kernel of L' is the set of pairwise sums of the six roots of the sextic B = λ_5^2 u^6 + λ_3^2 u^2 + λ_5 u + 1 = u·A(u) + 1, where A is the Bluher quintic of Part II; the proof is the identity L' = x^4 B^2 + B + 1. Hence the Frobenius permutes the six roots, its S_6-class is the factorisation type of B over F_q, the symplectic form is the duad–syntheme pairing of the generalised quadrangle W(2), and the one-parameter family L + εx^4 corresponds to uA(u) + √ε, interpolating between the quadratic sums of A_6 and the order-4 sums of X. The number of Frobenius-stable symplectic structures of each type is 28|t|/|C|. First moments of the family u^6 + a u^2 + b u + b^2 are proved; the eleven class counts are verified for q ≤ 512 (odd k) and new polynomials, depending on k mod 4, are given for even k (q ≤ 1024). The order-4 sums are treated as Frobenius traces of rank-4 Witt–Artin–Schreier sheaves. Using the hexad, a multiplicity formula for Witt traces along towers and the moduli of Gauss sums of Z/4-valued quadratic forms, it is proved that every individual sum S''(λ) is a rational integer, that the normalised Frobenius eigenvalues are roots of unity, that in the class of 5-cycles the L-polynomial is (1 − η^5 q^{5/2} T^5)/(1 − η q^{1/2} T) with η a primitive 8th root of unity, so that W' = −q^7 unconditionally (+q^7 for even k), that for the six classes whose kernel lies in F_{q^4} the sum over F_{q^12} equals q^4 times the sum over F_{q^4}, and that the remaining classes have all S'' = ±4q^6. The closed form X = q^6 + q^5 (odd k) is thereby reduced conditionally to the class counts and to the Brown invariants of explicit small-field Z/4-valued forms, both stated precisely and verified exactly. Contents: paper (LaTeX source and PDF, 30 pages, four figures), self-contained Python verification code (hexad search, sextic identity, class counts, Witt sums and L-polynomials, trace identities, stable symplectic structures), exact data for q ≤ 1024, and a results summary. Code: MIT; paper, data, figures: CC BY 4.0. Repository: https://github.com/Ruqing1963/legendre-intervals-part3

title: Reproducibility repository for "Edge-preserving Bayesian neural networks via hierarchical sparsity-promoting priors"
abstract: Recovering piecewise-smooth functions with jump discontinuities from noisy, indirect, and incomplete data is a central task in computational inverse problems. Bayesian neural networks (BNNs) with heavy-tailed weight priors have emerged as effective edge-preserving priors for such problems. However, posterior inference for these models remains computationally challenging, and existing approaches settle for point estimates obtained by directly optimizing heavy-tailed log-densities. We propose GSBL-BNNs, which model the neural network parameters hierarchically using sparsity-promoting priors from generalized sparse Bayesian learning (GSBL). The hierarchical formulation recovers several popular marginal priors, including Laplace and Student's $t$ (including Cauchy). A key modeling ingredient, novel among edge-preserving BNNs and native to the hierarchical formulation, couples each neuron's bias to its weights through a shared hyperparameter, so that the induced jump discontinuities are free to occur anywhere in the domain while the conditionally Gaussian structure underlying efficient inference is preserved. Furthermore, we develop a block-coordinate descent (BCD) algorithm for maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. This BCD approach alternates between standard network training with iteratively reweighted $\ell^2$-regularization and exact hyperparameter updates that are available in closed form for gamma and inverse gamma hyperpriors. Building on the BCD algorithm, we perform approximate Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification (UQ) using deep ensembles. Computational experiments---including signal denoising, deblurring, and inverting a two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation law---demonstrate that GSBL-BNNs deliver accurate edge-preserving reconstructions together with built-in UQ. Compared with Gaussian- and Cauchy-BNNs, they yield more accurate predictive means and avoid overconfident uncertainty estimates.

title: Effect of features burdened with classical error, misclassifications, Berkson error, and group-summary assignments on machine learning performance and interpretability
abstract: Abstract Measurement error is widespread in modern data pipelines, but its influence on predictive modeling and variable importance assessments in machine learning is often underestimated. Our study examines how input measurement error affects both prediction accuracy and interpretability across four common additive error types: classical error, misclassification of predictive features, Berkson error, caused by algorithmic or model-based assignment errors, and group-summary (aggregation) assignment errors. Using controlled Monte Carlo simulation experiments that cover regression and classification, we evaluate five popular machine learning models: generalized linear models, support vector machines, random forests, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptrons, across various error levels. To distinguish the effect of the error from optimization issues, hyperparameters are tuned separately for each dataset, and performance is measured using standard predictive metrics and permutation feature importance. Results show that measurement error generally reduces predictive performance and can significantly alter the ranking and estimated contribution of highly predictive features, with different degradation patterns depending on the error type and model. These findings clarify when performance declines might be mistaken for distributional shifts, among other things, and highlight the importance of diagnosing and correcting measurement error before drawing conclusions about model robustness, generalization, or variable relevance.

title: Learning Multimodal Sensor Fusion with JEPA Representations for Breathing Activity and Pose Recognition
abstract: Predictive video representations do not by themselves specify how a multimodal system should handle missing sensors. We transfer frozen V-JEPA2 features to a set of heterogeneous sensors comprised by RGB video, depth video, and radar time series. A shared fusion model uses modality queries, fixed sensor slots, and explicit availability to classify breathing activity and pose from all seven non-empty sensor subsets. The contribution is a controlled evaluation of subset supervision, pooling capacity, and representation transfer on 39 OMuSense-23 subjects with five subject-group folds and three seeds. With matched downstream parameter counts, the final model reaches recording-level activity macro-F1 of $75.23%\pm0.60$ averaged across seven subsets. Supervising all subsets in each batch improves the matched query-pooling control by 1.923 percentage points (conditional 95% subject-bootstrap interval [0.647, 3.209]), while query pooling shows no clear advantage over matched mean pooling under balanced supervision. Radar probes support transfer beyond pooled wavelet pixels, 64-token inference approximately preserves mean activity performance, and the tested Consensus-JEPA loss adds no measured benefit against its exact control.

title: TempoKV: Predictive KV Cache Quantization for Autoregressive Video Generation
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models enable streaming generation of long videos but suffer from significant memory overhead due to the rapidly growing KV cache. Existing KV cache quantization methods are primarily designed for LLMs and transfer poorly to video models, where activations exhibit different statistics and strong spatiotemporal redundancy. We observe that the video KV cache is largely predictable over time, with a clear asymmetry. Keys are highly predictable from their temporal history, while values depend primarily on the current key and need a short history of preceding values. Based on these observations, we propose \textbf{\method}, a training-free predictive KV cache quantization framework for AR video generation. \method predicts keys and values according to their distinct dependencies and stores only the residuals at low precision. Both predictors are lightweight, calibrated once offline by linear regression on a small set of BF16 samples, and remain fixed across prompts and generation runs. Experiments on Self-Forcing, Causal Forcing, and LongCat-Video-13B show that \method consistently achieves higher generation quality than existing KV cache quantization methods at comparable or higher compression ratios, reaching up to $6.71\times$ KV cache compression with the best overall quality--efficiency tradeoff. Our code will be released on GitHub.

title: No Such Code: Certified Invariants for Quantum Codes, Circuits, and Measurement
authors: The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics
abstract: Four questions sit at the base of fault-tolerant quantum computing: whether a code with given parameters can exist, whether two circuits denote the same operation, how much entropy a measurement irreversibly produces, and whether a compiled gate still means what it should. They are normally answered by four disjoint techniques. We show they are one technique. In each case the answer is an invariant—the object a governing transformation leaves fixed—and that invariant can be held as a certificate a proof kernel checks and an operator-native substrate computes. The instruments are the quantum weight enumerator, whose shadow variant yields what is, to our knowledge, the first machine-checked nonexistence certificate for a quantum error-correcting code (no pure [[4, 1, 3]] stabilizer code, reduced to an integer impossibility); the spider normal form, unique both as a linear map and as a content-addressed tree, at the minimal axiomatic footprint of a proof assistant; the measurement boundary defect, whose logical entropy equals a kernel-counted cohomology dimension; and the reduction receipt, round-tripping a certified gate word to bare metal on two independent substrates. Everything downstream of the explicitly labelled modeling step in each domain is exact integer or rational arithmetic. The common shape—find the invariant the transformation fixes, and read it off as a certificate—turns four hard quantum questions into arithmetic a machine can hold. Published by The Institute for Applied Ontological Mathematics.
